claims.claim: Auto Commit can stay checked on the PostgreSQL connection while tDBInput uses Use cursor with fetch size
claims.note: Wrong: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver only uses a server-side cursor (fetchSize) when auto-commit is off; with auto-commit on the whole result set is loaded into memory.

claims.note: Correct description of tSnowflakeOutput/tDBOutput(Snowflake) upsert mechanism.

Snowflake raises a nondeterministic MERGE error when the source has duplicate keys

claims.claim: With Die on error on every DB component the job exits non-zero after the mail is sent so TMC marks the run Failed

eval_critique: Assertion 9 (TMC execution statuses) is conditional and both answers satisfied it vacuously by never naming an API status constant; it only discriminates when an answer volunteers the wrong constant. Consider rewording so the answer must state how TMC reports the failed run (and optionally the API status) to make it non-vacuous.

Assertion 4 accepts 'upsert on order_id, batch size' OR 'staging + MERGE'; neither answer gave a numeric batch size for the Snowflake output, yet both pass via the alternative clause. If batch size matters, make it a separate assertion.
Assertion 8 was the only discriminator in this eval (without_skill set Auto Commit on while enabling Use cursor). Good catch; keep it.

No assertion checks the high-watermark safety design (upper bound taken from the source clock minus a lag, or an overlap) which both answers covered and which separates a restartable design from a naive max(updated_at) one.

No assertion checks that the watermark is written on the same connection/transaction as the load (atomicity), or that Allow parallel run is disabled for a 15-minute cadence; both are production-relevant and were covered by the with_skill answer and partially by without_skill.
